title: Automated Attestation Ledger for Data Residency & Retention Proofs
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Goal: Build an automated attestation ledger that produces tamper-evident proof bundles for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls tied to data residency and retention policies.

Scope:
- Control-to-artifact mapping for residency/retention controls (logical mapping layer).
- A lightweight, append-only ledger of attestations (proof bundles) consumed by auditors and downstream reporting.
- Snapshot collectors that harvest configuration and runtime artifacts (storage region tags, KMS keys, retention TTLs, access logs) and attach signed metadata.
- Automation for generating recurring reports and an API for on-demand proof retrieval.
- Integration points: Redwood Console (reporting page), evidence API, infra audit logs, Dedicated and Private deployments.

Out of scope for initial iteration: full block-chain style consensus, long-term archival policies beyond configured retention windows, interactive auditor UI (read-only endpoints only).
approach:
1) Design a control registry: create canonical mapping between SOC 2/ISO clauses and the artifacts we can collect (bucket region, retention TTL, KMS key alias, audit log shard).
2) Build Snapshot Collectors: small agents (k8s cronjobs and lambda tasks) that produce JSON proof artifacts with provenance metadata (collector id, timestamp, source-uri, sha256).
3) Attestation Ledger service: append-only storage for proofs (internally versioned, immutable object store with content-addressing). Ledger exposes an API to fetch proofs by control, tenant, and time window.
4) Sign and seal: proofs are signed by a Redwood KMS key; include a verification flow for auditors.
5) Reporting and exports: scheduled bundles, CSV/JSON downloads, and Console link with per-tenant proof summary.
6) Rollout: pilot with a small set of enterprise tenants and one Dedicated deployment to validate performance and privacy.

Design trade-offs considered: minimize PII in proofs by storing references to artifacts (uris + hashes) instead of raw logs; keep proofs small to favor fast retrieval; prefer KMS-based signing rather than external notary to reduce dependencies.
tasks: Write control mapping for SOC 2 CC6/CC7 and ISO 27001 A.8/A.12
Prototype collector for S3 buckets and storage retention settings
Define ledger schema and storage backend (object store with index)
Build sign/verify workflow using customer-specific KMS alias and Redwood signing key
Add Console UI surface for per-tenant proof summary and download
Create automated scheduler for weekly attestation bundles
acceptance_criteria: Control registry maps >=90% of residency/retention controls we test against (SOC 2, ISO 27001)
Snapshot collectors produce signed proof files with immutable sha256 and provenance metadata
Ledger API returns proofs within 500ms for tenant-level queries during pilot load
Proof bundles are downloadable and include verification steps documented in Confluence
Pilot tenant reports no PII leakage from proofs during security review
